summary:
AstroVital is an offline-first, autonomous health monitoring and medical decision-support web application designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) and NASA-STD-3001 clinical standards, the platform transforms complex physiological telemetry into an intuitive, interactive sci-fi medical command dashboard.

The software addresses the challenge by combining an interactive holographic anatomical body map with multi-modal data inputs, including manual biomarker logging, scenario simulators, and a simulated AI ocular and ultrasound scanner for Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS). Color-coded status nodes (Green, Amber, Red) allow astronauts to evaluate their cardiovascular, neurological, musculoskeletal, and immune health at a glance across four distinct mission environments (ISS, Lunar Gateway, Surface Rover, and Mars Habitat). It also features non-MD step-by-step self-examination guides, gamified daily health routines to combat checklist fatigue, an autonomous space pharmacy dispenser, and an asynchronous Deep Space Network (DSN) emergency SOS console that accounts for One-Way Light Time communication delays.

As humanity ventures toward the Moon and Mars, up to 22-minute signal delays make real-time reliance on Earth flight surgeons impossible. AstroVital empowers astronauts to autonomously detect anomalies early, execute NASA-validated countermeasures, and safeguard crew survival in deep space.
details:
Project Overview: What It Does & How It WorksAstrovital Space Health Monitor Systems (ASHM), developed by Team ORBITAL GATEWAY, is an offline-first, autonomous clinical decision-support and physiological telemetry platform designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) and NASA-STD-3001 clinical standards, ASHM transforms complex biomedical data into an actionable, interactive sci-fi medical command HUD.

ASHM operates through a four-stage autonomous workflow:

  1. Multi-Modal Data Ingestion: Astronauts input biomarkers through manual numerical entry (heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, daily sleep, radiation dosimetry), wearable telemetry simulation, or an onboard AI Ocular & Ultrasound HUD Scanner that evaluates retinal optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) for Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) and facial puffiness from cephalad fluid shifts.
  2. Holographic Anatomical Bio-Mapping: The software maps incoming vitals onto an interactive 2D/SVG human silhouette divided into four core physiological zones: Cardiovascular, Neuro-Ocular & Behavioral, Musculoskeletal, and Immune & Radiation. Each zone dynamically updates its color status (Green = Nominal, Amber = Advisory Monitor, Red = Critical Action Required) based on NASA HRP orbital safety corridors.
  3. Autonomous Countermeasure Prescription & Self-Exam Guidance: Clicking any body region displays plain-language, step-by-step diagnostic instructions for non-physician crew members, alongside specific NASA-validated countermeasures (e.g., ARED resistive loading, LBNP vacuum sessions, blue-spectrum circadian lighting, or Storm Shelter relocation) and an integrated ExMC Autonomous Space Pharmacy Dispenser.
  4. Asynchronous Deep-Space Telemetry & Emergency SOS: An environment selector dynamically recalibrates gravity fields, baseline radiation, and One-Way Light Time (OWLT) signal delays across four mission profiles: Low Earth Orbit (ISS - 0.2s), Lunar Gateway / Artemis (1.3s), Pressurized Surface Rover (4.5m), and Mars Transit / Habitat (up to 22m). During medical emergencies, the MCC-Houston SOS Console packages encrypted store-and-forward telemetry bundles for transmission via the Deep Space Network (DSN).

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Autonomous Crew Survival in Deep Space: On Artemis lunar surface operations and future Mars missions, communication blackouts and signal delays up to 22 minutes one-way eliminate real-time reliance on Earth-based Flight Surgeons. ASHM empowers astronauts to independently triage anomalies before they escalate into mission-threatening emergencies.
  • Reduced Cognitive Load: High-stress spaceflight environments cause checklist fatigue. By replacing dense medical tables with a color-coded anatomical hologram and real-time Lead-II ECG / SpO₂ oscilloscopes, astronauts can interpret their health status in seconds.
  • Preventive Health Engagement: Through a built-in gamification engine—complete with Sol streaks, XP progression, and daily countermeasure checklists—ASHM turns routine preventive care (like hydration, Vitamin D intake, and ARED workouts) into an engaging crew habit.
  • Earth-Based Spin-Off Impact: Beyond spaceflight, ASHM’s offline-first, store-and-forward telemedicine architecture can be directly adapted for remote terrestrial environments such as Antarctic research stations, submarines, offshore rigs, and rural disaster zones with limited internet connectivity.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend Architecture & Logic: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) engineered as an ultra-lightweight, zero-dependency single-page application (SPA) for instantaneous offline execution aboard spacecraft terminals.
  • UI Framework & Styling: Tailwind CSS for responsive dark-mode HUD styling, glassmorphism panels, and high-contrast clinical typography, paired with FontAwesome 6 vector iconography.
    • Chart.js: Powers the longitudinal mission health trend lines (tracking Cardiovascular Index, Bone Retention, and Circadian Sync across mission Sols) and the dynamic 5-Axis NASA HRP Hazard Radar Chart.
    • HTML5 Canvas API: Renders the real-time dual-channel oscillating ECG and SpO₂ Plethysmograph waveforms that dynamically shift frequency and color during tachycardia or radiation alerts.
    • Interactive Vector Graphics (SVG): Custom-coded anatomical body map with CSS laser-scanline animations and reactive DOM state bindings.
  • Deployment & Version Control: Git and GitHub Pages for public cloud hosting and rapid cross-platform accessibility.

How the Project Is Creative

  • bridging the "Non-MD Gap": Most health dashboards assume clinical expertise. ASHM integrates a dedicated "Crew Self-Exam & Escalation Guide" directly beside every organ system, teaching astronauts how to position an ultrasound probe or brachial cuff in microgravity, why the physiological shift occurs, and exact numerical thresholds for escalating to MCC-Houston.
  • Dynamic Environment-Aware Hazard Matrix: Rather than treating "space" as a single static environment, ASHM dynamically links NASA’s 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, and Hostile Closed Environments) to the crew’s current vehicle or habitat, automatically adjusting both the 5-axis radar chart and communication latency timers.
  • Interactive Scenario & Pharmacy Simulation: Judges and users do not need medical hardware to test the software; built-in one-click mission scenarios (Nominal Day, SANS & Sleep Deficit, and Solar Particle Event) and an interactive ExMC Space Pharmacy let users trigger anomalies and watch countermeasures actively restore crew vitals in real time.

Factors Considered by Team ORBITAL GATEWAY

  1. The 5 NASA HRP Spaceflight Hazards: Every metric and alert threshold was mapped directly to NASA’s official Human Research Program risks, including Spaceflight Osteopenia (1–1.5% monthly bone loss), SANS ocular globe flattening, GCR/SPE radiation spikes, circadian misalignment, and cabin $pp\text{CO}_2$ toxicity.
  2. Signal Latency & Offline Reliability: Recognizing that cloud-dependent apps fail in deep space, we designed ASHM to run 100% locally in the browser while simulating realistic store-and-forward telemetry packet compression for asynchronous Flight Surgeon review.
  3. Human Factors & Spacecraft Ergonomics: We utilized a dark-adapted, high-contrast color palette (deep space slate with emerald, amber, and rose semantic indicators) to minimize astronaut eye strain during dim cabin shifts and emergency red-alert states.
